text:
anna-sales: Heads up — AcmeHealth is blocked on the POC. Their calls are getting 403s with an 'invalid org' message, then a bunch of retries hit 429s. They need help reproducing and a short workaround so the demo tomorrow isn't blocked. @carla-se
acme-ops: repro steps below, tried curl and our SDK. Copy/paste: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}'``` Response: `{
  "error": "invalid_org_claim",
  "message": "org claim does not match resource binding"
}` Also saw `429` after 10 quick retries.
carla-se: thanks — can you paste the full request headers (redact keys) and the token metadata from your key management UI? quick guess: looks like a project-scoped key being used for an org-scoped endpoint.
acme-ops: headers (redacted): `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX`, `User-Agent: acme-sdk/2.1.0`, `X-Project-ID: proj-abc123` No `X-ORG-ID` header. Token metadata from our portal: `scopes: ["generate:read"], bound_to: project:proj-abc123`
ben-eng: yep that matches — the key is project-bound, but your demo host is calling the org-level endpoint. Two options: 1) call the project-scoped endpoint `https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/proj-abc123/generate` OR 2) create an org-scoped key/rotate to a key that binds to the org. Missing `X-ORG-ID` will trigger `invalid_org_claim`.
edith-support: small note on the 429s — the SDK retries rapidly by default which will push you into rate limits if the first requests 403. Please enable exponential backoff (SDK v2.1.1+ default) or add `Retry-After` handling. Also enable debug logs with `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1` to capture the header set by the SDK.
acme-ops: ah ok. We were using `acme-sdk/2.1.0` — upgrading to `2.1.2` now. Quick Q: is there any temporary workaround other than rotating keys? We want to keep the same key for the demo.
ben-eng: temp workaround: hit the project-scoped endpoint (quick change in config) — that will accept project-bound keys immediately. Example: ```bash curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/proj-abc123/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi"}'``` No rotation needed.
carla-se: also adding note on pricing/entitlements — project-bound keys are standard for demo sandboxes. If you want an org-level key for cross-project demos we can issue one for the trial (short TTL) — I'll coordinate with sales ops.
acme-ops: switching endpoint now... tests green! 200s returning, content looks good. Sorry about the noise with retries earlier.
deploy-bot: [infra] detected spike: 10x 403->retry->429 pattern from ip 52.45.12.9 in us-west-2, flagged as transient request storm.
dmitri-ml: fyi — if you're doing evals with long-ish sequences, consider enabling prefix caching on the deployment to cut token cost. Not urgent for demo.
anna-sales: amazing — thanks team. acme wants an ask: can we get a short note on recommended dev setup and whether a dedicated trial (burst capacity) makes sense for their demo traffic? They also need a line for their security questionnaire re: key binding behavior.
carla-se: I'll write up a 1-page FAQ: how keys bind (org vs project), recommended endpoints, SDK versions, and a suggested demo traffic plan (bursting + backoff). Will include a templated response for the security questionnaire about token scoping and rotation.
edith-support: opening ticket SUP-12345, attaching logs and remediation steps. I'll mark it P0 for tomorrow's demo window and cc sales-ops.
acme-ops: thanks everyone — demo looks solid now. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
anna-sales: closing loop on our side after carla posts the FAQ. :thumbsup:
